Consistency across renderings of one organisation

Source: R/truth.R
pf_consistency.Rd

A ground-truth-free quality metric. One organisation is written many ways across grants; grouping those renderings by address is independent of the name comparator, so within a group every rendering should receive the same EIN whatever that EIN turns out to be. Disagreement inside a group is a defect regardless of which member is right.

Usage

pf_consistency(run, groups = NULL, min_size = 2L)

Arguments

run

A run result, as for pf_evaluate().

groups

(grant_id, group_id) from dev/build-triangulation-sample.R, or a path to it.

min_size

Smallest group to score. Default 2.

Value

A list of summary and detail (per group), class pf_consistency.

Details

That independence from ground truth is the point. The anchor-based labels in PF-TRUTH-TRIANGULATED.csv measured only ~50-60% precise, because a shared street address also covers fiscal sponsors (MULTIPLIERORG and the Natural Resources Defense Council), individual payees at an organisation's address (EDUCATIONAL GRANT - <person>), and cases where the anchoring YES is itself wrong (Homes for our Troops). None of that damages a disagreement count: those groups are noisy in every configuration, so comparing configurations on the same groups still isolates the change.

It is necessary, not sufficient. A configuration that answers every rendering identically and wrongly scores perfectly here, so read it alongside pf_evaluate(), never instead of it.
